root_cause.primary: The final non-core wrapper envelope, gpu_capacity=1 with gpu_memory_utilization=0.99, still leaves zero GPU KV cache blocks for Llama-2 7B, one-group TP4, 500 real remote adapters on 4x24GB RTX 3090.
not_primary: Not remote artifact failure: all 500 adapters were fetched from the real remote endpoint.
Not host OOM: adapter loading completed, placement completed, and the process exited through the same vLLM ValueError before HTTP readiness.
Not CUDA OOM: there is no CUDA out-of-memory traceback and all GPUs returned to 15MiB after cleanup.
Not a measured replay-quality result: no HTTP readiness and no replay request.
root_cause.mechanism: The zero-cache-block failure persists after exhausting wrapper-only memory-envelope levers used in this campaign: DP2/TP2 failed on startup host memory, G1/TP4 loaded 500 adapters but had zero GPU blocks at gpu_memory_utilization=0.88, still zero at 0.95, still zero after lowering gpu_capacity to 2, and still zero at minimal gpu_capacity=1 with gpu_memory_utilization=0.99.
root_cause.why_not_patch_core: Making this fit would require changing dLoRA/vLLM cache allocation, adapter placement, quantization, rank layout, or model/adapter memory management. Those are core implementation changes outside the allowed fair adaptation boundary.

decision.reason: The 7B formal gate cannot reach HTTP readiness under the unchanged 500-adapter true-remote workload and the final wrapper-only envelope, so launching the 4000-request replay would not produce a valid e2e_v3 result.
decision.paper_use: Do not enter dLoRA as a full 3B+7B formal comparison row on this 4x3090 machine. Keep the successful 3B migration_type=3 full replay as appendix or limited single-backbone evidence, and cite this 7B infeasibility gate when explaining exclusion from the main combined table.
